name: ** Product Manager, Digital Banking Division
goals: * Launch card-based campaigns fast, keep integration overhead low, avoid engineering escalations reaching her desk
**Frustrations:** Feature requests to Interswitch take multiple cycles to be scoped; no visibility into API roadmap; limit changes require full card reissuance
**Behaviors:** Reviews API changelogs monthly, escalates to account manager when a workaround costs her team more than two engineering days
**Needs:** Predictable roadmap communication, ability to adjust card controls without reissuance, clear SLAs for feature requests
**Quote:** "I don't need more features. I need to stop being the translator between my engineers and your support team."
**Jobs to be Done:** When rolling out a new card-based product, I want to configure and adjust card behavior without engineering rework, so I can hit launch dates without escalation.

name: ** Operations Lead, Card Services
goals: * Resolve fraud and dispute cases quickly, minimize customer complaint escalations to his desk
**Frustrations:** Delay between freeze confirmation and scheme-level enforcement; disputes where the timeline doesn't match what the dashboard shows
**Behaviors:** Monitors the ops dashboard multiple times a day, personally handles high-severity fraud escalations
**Needs:** Real-time confirmation that a freeze is actually enforced at the scheme level, audit trail timestamps that match reality
**Quote:** "When I tell a customer their card is frozen, it needs to actually be frozen. Right now I'm not always telling the truth."
**Jobs to be Done:** When fraud is reported, I want the freeze to take effect instantly and verifiably, so I can protect the customer and defend the bank's position in a dispute.

name: ** Chief Technology Officer, mid-stage fintech
goals: * Ship integrations fast with minimal back-and-forth, keep infrastructure lean, avoid building workaround systems for gaps in vendor APIs
**Frustrations:** No webhooks force polling architecture; ambiguous error codes require manual log correlation with Interswitch support; unreliable sandbox breaks CI/CD
**Behaviors:** Evaluates competing middleware providers annually, makes build-vs-workaround calls based on engineering hours lost per quarter
**Needs:** Event-driven architecture support (webhooks), structured error responses, stable sandbox parity with production
**Quote:** "Every workaround we build for your API is a workaround we're stuck maintaining forever."

**Jobs to be Done:** When integrating card lifecycle events into our product, I want event-driven notifications instead of polling, so I can build a responsive customer experience without wasting API calls.

name: ** Compliance Officer, fintech card program
goals: * Produce accurate, complete audit documentation on demand, avoid manual data reconciliation
**Frustrations:** No self-serve log export; dependent on Interswitch support turnaround during audit windows; keeps a shadow spreadsheet to compensate
**Behaviors:** Runs a quarterly audit prep cycle, escalates to account management two weeks before CBN deadlines
**Needs:** Self-serve, filterable export of issuance and status logs, exportable in audit-ready format
**Quote:** "I shouldn't need a support ticket to prove we're compliant."

**Jobs to be Done:** When preparing for a CBN audit, I want to independently pull card issuance and status logs by date range, so I can complete the audit report without depending on vendor turnaround.

name: Data User
goals: Improve data experience
frustrations:
**Transcript:**
> **Interviewer:** Think of the most painful part of your current workflow. Can you describe a specific moment when that pain showed up?
>
> **Interviewee:** Every CBN audit cycle. I need issuance and status logs for a specific date range. There's no self-serve way to get that — I open a support ticket and wait.
>
> **Interviewer:** How long does that usually take?
>
> **Interviewee:** Anywhere from two to five business days, depending on how backed up support is. If the audit deadline is tight, that's genuinely stressful.
>
> **Interviewer:** What do you do to work around it?
>
> **Interviewee:** I keep my own shadow spreadsheet, updated manually, so I'm not fully dependent on their turnaround. It's extra work I shouldn't have to do.
>
> **Interviewer:** What would need to be true for this not to be a problem?
>
> **Interviewee:** A dashboard where I filter by date range and export the log myself. I don't need anything fancy. I need independence from the ticket queue.
behaviors: Interacts with data features
